title: Gravity Duel: Orbital Combat
shortDescription: Bend missile paths around planets, outmaneuver rivals, and turn gravity into your weapon.
description:
Gravity Duel: Orbital Combat is a space arena shooter where the best shot is not always a straight line. Fly independently of your aim, curve missiles around celestial bodies, and use moving cover to attack from unexpected angles. Watch out: your own returning missiles can be dangerous too.

Progress through 30 distinct arenas across three units. Begin with planets and moons, then face multi-star systems and neutron-star beams. Later, black holes pull your ship as well as your shots, while wormholes carry both ships and missiles across the arena. Early levels teach the basics before these hazards combine into more demanding battles.

Fight duels, survive four-way free-for-all rounds, take on two coordinated AI rivals, and challenge a different Boss at the end of each unit. Collect six tactical pickups: trajectory guidance, a shield, heavy shells, a laser, homing missiles, and long-lasting orbital shots. Victory comes from positioning, timing, and choosing how to use the arena.

Play the solo campaign, find an online match, or invite friends to a room for up to four players. Online battles offer four-way free-for-all and 2-vs-2 teams, with AI filling empty seats. Each round has no respawns; the last surviving pilot or team scores, and the first to three wins the match.
controls: Desktop: WASD to move; mouse to aim; left click or Space to fire; P or Esc to pause. Mobile: left stick to move; right stick to aim, then release to fire. A shot released during reload waits until ready. Start a new aim to replace that queued shot, or return the right stick to its center before release to cancel.
reviewerNotes:
Submitted with the subtitle Orbital Combat because the previous rejected record still reserves the original title. This is an improved resubmission of the same project, not an unrelated game.

This is a substantially revised resubmission of Gravity Duel (previous game ID 7917913a-5362-40b8-bb6b-7965951f2ad5). Changes include sharper procedural visuals, independent movement/aiming, mobile dual-stick release-to-fire controls, 30 distinct arenas, progressive AI and coordinated squads, four-way survival battles, three solo Boss encounters, and online friend/random rooms.

The opening levels intentionally introduce the mechanics gradually. Unit 1 has 7 levels with planets/moons only; unit 2 has 10 levels adding stars and neutron stars; unit 3 has 13 levels adding black holes, ship gravity and wormholes. Each unit ends with four-way survival, a 1-vs-2 AI squad, then an additional Boss. The level picker previews later arenas, but the submitted solo campaign unlocks one level at a time and has no unlock-all or practice-all button.

Only the new independent movement/aiming controls are exposed. Old same-keyboard two-player and CLASSIC control modes are unavailable. Online uses one device per player, 2 to 4 humans, with AI filling remaining seats; Bosses are solo only. This is a Basic Launch build with CrazyGames SDK Data save and audio mute support, and no advertising requests. The public GitHub playtest has a separate practice-all option for reviewing later content; it is absent from the submission build.
status: Prepared copy; not yet submitted. Multiplayer must pass final platform preview QA.
